find:
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION updater.guard_passkey_registration_open() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER
replace:
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION updater.guard_passkey_registration_open() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql
why: the guard fires for the web login, which holds five columns of the open-registration table and none of the limits table; as an invoker body every web insert would fail with permission denied (measured, not assumed)

replace: SELECT count(*)::integer INTO existing_rows FROM updater.passkey_registrations r
why: the per-digest row cap is a read-then-write; without the transaction-scoped advisory lock 50 concurrent registrations each count zero rows and all 50 land (measured: 50 rows, cap of 4 never consulted)
a registration row must be accepted only for a digest the updater opened; a page that saw the URL fragment must not be able to insert for a registration nobody issued
a registration is single-use: once the updater has consumed R a late insert must be refused, or a second passkey can be created from a spent secret
R lives 30 minutes (design 5.1) and the comparison is against the DATABASE clock, so a caller-supplied time cannot extend it
a replayed approval must be a no-op: without the RETURNING clause a bot re-POSTing one stale assertion becomes 10000 journal lines (design 13 P8)
the bucket is the DATABASE's hour; a fixed bucket would let a caller open a second aggregate for an hour that already has one (P-3)
delivery is one-way, or a re-drive that failed halfway puts the same hour back in the queue and the owner sees the line twice (P-4)
the aggregate rises by one or not at all, so no caller can rewrite an hour's count and hide how many attempts failed
a passkey add with nobody to warn must refuse loudly rather than report a warning that was never sent (design 5.1 step 7, P-5)
the idempotency key is the whole of the re-drive safety; a key that varies per call lets a retried add tell the owner twice about the same key (R14c, P-5)
the consumed marker is what makes a late web insert fail by name; a deleted row makes it look merely expired
the options object is what the owner is shown; only the updater's ledger may decide what it says, and only consumed_at may move
a web-inserted push rendering as the updater is the one impersonation the root-only VAPID key was changed to stop (R12)

find:
GRANT SELECT (registration_digest, mode, options_json, authorization_challenge, expires_at)
  ON updater.passkey_open_registrations TO control_room_private_web;
replace: GRANT SELECT ON updater.passkey_open_registrations TO control_room_private_web;
why: the web's reach here is five columns and no more; consumed_at and installation_id are the updater's, and a table-wide grant would hand them over silently
